h1: Anda Resort Koh Lipe — Wooden Bungalows on Sunrise Beach Where You Step Straight Onto the Sand
intro: Koh Lipe has only a handful of beachfront stays on Sunrise Beach that are still affordable, and Anda Resort is one of them · a 3-star boutique resort sitting right on the white-sand, clear-water beach on the sunrise side of the island · with Thai-Balinese wooden rooms and bungalows, a swimming pool, a beachfront restaurant, and only about a 5-minute walk to the island's Walking Street · rates start at around ฿2,200/night for a standard room, making it a go-to when you want a beachfront location without paying pool-villa prices.

Outdoor swimming pool with wooden deck and sun loungers at Anda Resort
Beachfront restaurant and bar looking out over the clear water of Sunrise Beach and nearby islands

body.html: Sunrise Beach is the stretch many travellers rate as the prettiest on Koh Lipe — fine white sand, water clear enough to spot coral, and one of the island's best sunrise spots · Anda Resort sits directly on it, with some rooms opening straight onto the sand · this is the first thing almost every review mentions: a beachfront location a step from the water, at a fraction of what the luxury stays on the same beach charge.

Rooms come in several tiers to suit your budget · Standard and Thai Hill Side are the smaller, value rooms set back from the beach · Superior Balcony and Deluxe Sea View add a balcony and sea views · and the top pick is the Deluxe Beach Front Villa, a roughly 35 sqm wooden bungalow on the sand with the beach at your door · the woodwork and Thai-Balinese décor give it a traditional island-resort feel rather than a sleek modern look · many reviews say the rooms are bigger than expected, though a few are starting to show their age, so check the photos for the exact tier you book.
"Opened the door in the morning and the sea was right there, the water so clear, just a few steps to the waterline — a location like this at this price is hard to find on Koh Lipe."

Shared facilities include a swimming pool with a wooden deck (open roughly 9am to 6pm) and a beachfront restaurant and bar looking out over the beach and nearby islands — dinner with a drink and a sea view is a favourite here · the menu runs Thai, international and seafood, and several reviews single out the curries and pad thai · breakfast scores middling, decent but not a wide spread · free coffee and tea are available in the restaurant during the day, but rooms have no in-room tea/coffee set, a point some guests flag.

Location is the main draw · it's about a 5-minute walk to Walking Street, the island's central lane lined with restaurants, mini-marts, tour desks and dive shops · Pattaya Beach and Sunset Beach are roughly a 10–15 minute walk away · the resort has snorkelling off its beach, on-site massage, and helps arrange boat tours and ferry tickets · staff earn praise for being friendly and helpful, especially with pier transfers.

To be straight with you, Anda isn't flawless on every front · the recurring complaint is thin walls — you can hear neighbours, and families with children stay here often · beach sun loungers are limited, so latecomers may miss out · and platform scores diverge sharply: Trip.com sits around 8.8 while TripAdvisor averages 3.0/5, which tells you the experience swings by room and season · this is a resort that's worth it when the price is right rather than one that guarantees brilliance across the board.

The takeaway from real guest reviews: if you're coming to Koh Lipe to focus on the sea, snorkelling and a beachfront room at an accessible price, Anda delivers that well · but if you're expecting honeymoon-level quiet or brand-new rooms, look one tier up · the trick is to book a Sea View or Beach Front room to make staying on this beach worthwhile, while the inland Standard rooms suit travellers who just want a budget base close to the water.

honestSummary: Anda Resort Koh Lipe is a Sunrise Beach stay that delivers a beachfront location at an accessible price — ideal if you're here for the sea, snorkelling and a room near the water without paying pool-villa rates · but accept that the walls are thin, some rooms are ageing, and the experience swings by room and season, so it's a place that's worth it when the price is right rather than a guaranteed standout on every front.
honestChecks: If you want honeymoon-level quiet — the walls are thin and families with children stay often → choose an adults-focused stay or a private pool villa on the island instead.

If you're paying to be on the beach but book an inland room — Standard/Thai Hill Side rooms sit back with no sea view → upgrade to a Deluxe Sea View or Beach Front Villa to make this beach worthwhile.
If you're planning the low season (May–Oct) — Koh Lipe's monsoon is strong, many places close and ferries run less → confirm the resort is open and check the boat schedule before you book.

tips.title: Upgrade to a sea-view or beachfront room
tips.body: If you're staying on the beach, pick a Deluxe Sea View or Beach Front Villa — it's worth more than an inland Standard room with no view of the water.

tips.title: Ask for a room away from the family zone
tips.body: Walls are thin and families with kids stay often. When booking, ask for an upper-floor or quieter room away from the busy area.

tips.title: Let the resort handle the boats
tips.body: Staff help book ferry tickets and pier transfers. Tell them your arrival and departure boats in advance for the smoothest trip.

tips.title: Avoid low season, check the boat schedule
tips.body: Best time is Nov–Apr with calm, clear seas. The rainy season (May–Oct) brings strong monsoon, many places close and ferries run less — always check first.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Anda Resort Koh Lipe

faq.q: Where is Anda Resort Koh Lipe and how do you get there?
faq.a: It sits right on Sunrise Beach, Koh Lipe, Satun Province · about a 5-minute walk to the island's central Walking Street · to reach Koh Lipe you take a boat from Pak Bara Pier (Satun) or a pier in a nearby province, then a longtail to the beach · the resort can arrange ferry tickets and pier transfers — ask in advance.

faq.q: What are Anda Resort's starting rates and room types?
faq.a: From around ฿2,200/night for a Standard Room · Superior Balcony about ฿2,900 · Deluxe Sea View about ฿3,600 · and the top Deluxe Beach Front Villa (~35 sqm, on the sand) about ฿4,800 · rates swing by season and climb at peak, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Anda Resort best for?
faq.a: Best for travellers focused on the sea and snorkelling who want a beachfront room at an accessible price · the Sunrise Beach location makes Walking Street an easy walk · if you want honeymoon-level quiet or brand-new rooms, a higher-tier stay may suit you better, as the walls are thin and families with children stay often.

faq.q: What is Sunrise Beach in front of Anda Resort like, can you swim?
faq.a: Sunrise Beach has fine white sand, clear water with visible coral, and you can swim · it's one of the island's best sunrise spots · there's snorkelling off the beach in front of the resort, though beach sun loungers are limited so latecomers may miss out.

faq.q: Why do Anda Resort's scores differ across sites?
faq.a: Because the experience swings by room and season · Trip.com sits around 8.8 while TripAdvisor averages 3.0/5 · the recurring complaints are thin walls and some ageing rooms · it's a place that's worth it when the price is right and you book a sea-view tier or above, rather than a guaranteed standout on every front.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Anda Resort?
faq.a: Best is November to April with calm, clear seas and clear skies · the rainy season (May–Oct) brings strong monsoon, many island places close and ferries run less often, so always confirm the resort is open and check the boat schedule before booking.
